method: Five parallel agents scanned every page (source docs, generated HTML, builders, data, diagrams) for overlap that should collapse to ONE canonical home, so each concept has a single update site. PLAN ONLY — nothing is merged until you approve a candidate.
framing: The wiki is better-architected than it feels: most apparent duplication is intentional, already single-sourced data-driven VIEWS (catalog ↔ doc ↔ matrix off one JSON). The real maintenance hazard is narrower: (a) hand-copied numeric tables in generated pages that should render from the canonical JSON; (b) a few concepts genuinely written out 2–3× in the numbered spec spine; (c) framing/boilerplate restated across sibling pages. Risk tag: low = generated pages / data only; med = touches one numbered doc lightly; high = edits the 01–19 spec spine (DOCMAP + 900+ Doc NN refs).

findings.title: Pillar roster + ordering lives in 5 places
findings.overlap: The 12 pillar codes/names appear in 5 authored places — and README/conventions §3.4 order (CV,MET,REN,HEP,INF,HEM,ENDO,BCM,NUT,SLP,FIT,MCS) DISAGREES with Doc 03 §3.1 (sorted by weight). Same set, two orders = live desync hazard.
findings.canonical: README §3.4 + data/pillars.json own the roster + binding order.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (Doc 02 keeps definitions but cites §3.4 for order; generated tables render from pillars.json)
findings.gain: One binding roster/order; removes the README-vs-Doc03 ordering mismatch.

findings.title: Doc 13 ↔ Doc 14 validation duplication
findings.overlap: Discrimination, calibration, fairness, drift and the SHIP/NO-SHIP gate are each defined near-verbatim in BOTH docs (Doc 14 claims to 'extend' Doc 13 but re-specifies the shared metrics). A tolerance change (e.g. ECE ≤ 0.05) must be edited in 2–3 places today.
findings.canonical: Doc 13 = canonical for metric definitions; Doc 14 keeps only the genuine 2.0 parts (validation-objects, synthetic generator, early-warning eval, executable harness, honest status).
findings.mechanism: fold (Doc 14 §3/§4/§6/§8/§9 → 'as Doc 13 §4.x, plus [2.0 delta]' pointers)
findings.gain: Single home per validation metric. Highest payoff, highest blast — preserve section anchors.

findings.title: Wearable trust-tier (D22) table copied 4×
findings.overlap: The 3-tier q_source mapping (clinical 0.85–1.0 / consumer 0.6–0.8 / inferential = informational) + the 'needs clinical-grade confirm before red' rule is stated four times; q_source values still await calibration, so the four copies will silently desync.
findings.canonical: appendix-wearables (the 14-row data-driven catalog) owns the table; Doc 07 §2 keeps the 3-row narrative; Doc 06 §2 drops its inline copy and cites it.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer
findings.gain: One update site for the tier values.

findings.title: Hand-copied numeric tables that should be JSON views
findings.overlap: The scoring-constants table (φ, κ_resp, γ, δ, ρ_k, R_crit, cap…) and the pillar base-weights W_k are restated literally in admin-weights + overview rather than rendered from data/constants.json / pillar-weights.json — exactly the drift the JSON-canonical rule (D32) exists to prevent.
findings.canonical: data/constants.json + data/pillar-weights.json (machine); Doc 03 the authored mirror.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (generated pages render from JSON)
findings.gain: Removes 2–3 hand-maintained copies of each numeric table.

findings.title: Gaps/review pages: 5 lenses, framing restated 5×
findings.overlap: These are five genuinely distinct axes (app surface / buildability / cohesion / questionnaire coverage / clinician red-team) — NOT content duplicates. But the axis legend, the 'Illustrative §5.6' callout, and the 4×4 sibling cross-ref scaffolding are restated on every one.
findings.canonical: chapter-7 landing = the one place that explains the 5-axis taxonomy; each page keeps its own findings.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (shared callout + sibling-xref into one builder snippet; hub owns the legend)
findings.gain: One home for the taxonomy framing; do NOT merge the views.

sections.title: Low risk — generated pages / data only

findings.title: Onboarding gating vs Eligibility & gating
findings.overlap: Both explain how onboarding answers gate downstream questions (both read question-bank.json gating metadata).
findings.canonical: eligibility-gating owns the gating-rule semantics; onboarding keeps only the first-run sequence/UX.
findings.mechanism: fold (move the 'how gating works' explanation into eligibility-gating)
findings.gain: Removes the double-explanation of the same gating mechanism.

findings.title: feedback-loop hard-codes its action list
findings.overlap: The demo's 5 ACTIONS are the same as Doc 11 §8 but hard-coded inline (engine constants are already sourced from PURESCORE_DATA; the action list is not).
findings.canonical: Doc 11/Doc 12 own the action library.
findings.mechanism: fold (source the demo's action subset from data, like the constants already are)
findings.gain: Demo labels/effects can't drift from the canonical library.

findings.title: Persona attributes stored in two JSONs
findings.overlap: The same 13 clinical personas' attributes (age/meds/multipliers/notes) are restated in both JSONs; the matrix is a legitimate second view (inference) but shouldn't re-store the descriptive fields.
findings.canonical: personas.json owns persona attributes; persona-matrix.json references ids + owns only the inference layer.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (de-dup the JSON; keep both pages)
findings.gain: One edit site for persona age/meds/multipliers.

findings.title: uber-map vs calc-uber — NOT a dup (label fix)
findings.overlap: Suspected duplicate, but they are distinct (live Calculation Explorer vs static 5-view architecture diagram). The real defect: index.html lists uber-map TWICE under two names, and the two pages' titles are confusingly similar.
findings.canonical: Keep both pages.
findings.mechanism: label cleanup (dedupe the index cards; give distinct one-line descriptors)
findings.gain: Removes the strongest 'are these the same page?' confusion.

findings.title: chapter-0 landing ≈ index.html
findings.overlap: chapter-0 (Start-here landing) is a thin auto-generated subset of what index.html already does richer — two 'Start here' homes.
findings.canonical: index.html is the home.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (point chapter-0 at index, or slim it — it's the one landing that competes with Home)
findings.gain: Removes a near-redundant orientation page.

findings.title: SI-units blurb duplicated
findings.overlap: The SI unit-conversion explanation appears in both pages (both over data/units.json).
findings.canonical: reference-range-resolver owns the units explanation.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer
findings.gain: One home for the units blurb.

sections.title: Medium risk — touches a numbered doc lightly

findings.title: purescore-sex restates Doc 08 bands
findings.overlap: The sex page restates Doc 08's reference cut-points (Total-T, HDL-M/F, waist, Hgb, FSH/AMH…) as a male/female toggle; the gated-question list (6 male + 21 female) is its unique value.
findings.canonical: Doc 08 owns the bands/stage models.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (strip restated bands → Doc 08 §5 refs; keep the toggle UI + gated questions)
findings.gain: One place to re-verify sex bands on cadence.

findings.title: Action id namespaces collide (ADH-)
findings.overlap: Three id systems describe the same actions; Doc 12 uses ADH-MET/ADH-STATIN while adherence.json uses ADH-001… — same prefix, unrelated meaning (a real correctness seam), with goals linking adherence ids.
findings.canonical: Doc 12 = the action library; adherence/goals reference its ids.
findings.mechanism: id-reconciliation + crosswalk (give check-ins a non-colliding prefix or map each to a Doc 12 action id) — do NOT merge the three
findings.gain: One canonical id per real-world action across catalogue/check-in/goal.

findings.title: class-model (object) vs dossier-erd (entity) can desync
findings.overlap: dossier-erd is 'one table per class' over the same class spec class-model renders; per-class field lists are restated, so a field change needs two edits.
findings.canonical: class-model is the object-model source; ERD/c4/api/sequences/stories are downstream views.
findings.mechanism: single-spec guard (verify build_grid_erd generates FROM the class spec, not a parallel hand-list) — no page merge
findings.gain: Prevents field-level drift between object and entity models.

findings.title: Care pages duplicate Doc 11 §9 delivery / Doc 16 §2 escalation
findings.overlap: prevention-engagement's reminder/alert framework restates Doc 11 §9 delivery (the page itself says reminders should route through §9, not a parallel sender), and care escalation overlaps Doc 16 §2 tiers + the PHQ-9→C-SSRS gate. The 3 care pages among themselves are NOT duplicates (clean facets).
findings.canonical: Doc 11 §9 = delivery mechanism; Doc 16 §2 = escalation authority.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (make the existing 'route through §9' / 'escalation per §2' pointers binding; no new C-SSRS logic in care pages)
findings.gain: Stops a second nudge-sender and a second escalation spec from drifting.

findings.title: consent-onboarding ↔ Doc 16 §4 not bound
findings.overlap: The interactive consent prototype enacts exactly Doc 16 §4's policy (granular consent, genetic/reproductive handling, withdrawal, legal basis, audit) but doesn't visibly cite it as its spec.
findings.canonical: Doc 16 §4 = canonical policy; the prototype is its UX instantiation.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (add 'implements Doc 16 §4' binding; align the data classes/purposes 1:1) — do NOT merge (standalone page)
findings.gain: Prototype can't drift from the governing policy.

findings.title: Missing-coverage residual lists in 2–3 formats
findings.overlap: The 'specified-but-not-built / missing markers & gates' backlog (ethnicity gate, G6PD, unit-error detection, calibration constants, Gulf-Arab cut-points) is enumerated in both the data-driven coverage register and Doc 17 §K narrative.
findings.canonical: data/coverage.json = machine source for clinical-coverage gaps.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (Doc 17 §K references the register rather than re-listing)
findings.gain: Backlog stops drifting between a JSON page and a hand-maintained §K.

sections.title: High risk — edits the numbered spec spine (01–19)

findings.title: Marker band VALUES authored in Doc 02 AND the JSON
findings.overlap: Per-pillar band values (e.g. SBP 90–119/120–139/≥140) are authored in both Doc 02 prose and range-variations.json/Appendix A; range variations are single-sourced but the base bands are not.
findings.canonical: range-variations.json / Appendix A own the values; Doc 02 = pedagogy + illustrative bands.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer + a build-time reconcile check (like _engine_guard) — do NOT bulk-delete Doc 02 tables (load-bearing teaching content)
findings.gain: Removes silent Doc-02-vs-JSON band drift.

findings.title: Empirical-Bayes baseline (z_i) formula written twice
findings.overlap: The shrinkage baseline μ_i^p and z_i = (x−μ)/σ are fully written out in both docs with near-identical prose; the two distinct USES (score-entry vs early-warning) are legitimate.
findings.canonical: Doc 03 §2b owns the formula; Doc 05 §5.1 points to it and keeps only the early-warning framing.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer
findings.gain: One home for the baseline formula.

findings.title: Companion-vector table duplicated in Doc 03
findings.overlap: Doc 03 §2b.1 prints a 9-row companion-vector table that is a near-subset of Doc 05 §4 — and Doc 03 itself says 'the full set is defined in Doc 05 §4'.
findings.canonical: Doc 05 §4 owns the companion vector.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (trim Doc 03 §2b.1 to the 2 dims that re-enter the score; pointer for the rest)
findings.gain: Removes a 9-row table one section before its canonical home.

findings.title: Release-gate (Go/No-Go) block triplicated
findings.overlap: The SHIP-only-if gate is written out three times; Doc 16 §8 is the governance-complete version (adds owners + Oversight Board).
findings.canonical: Doc 16 §8 = canonical gate registry.
findings.mechanism: canonical+pointer (Doc 13 §4.6 / Doc 14 §9 → 'see Doc 16 §8 G1–G12' + doc-local nuance only) — preserve G-ids (load-bearing refs)
findings.gain: One place to change a release-gate criterion.
